newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvians say no crisis as key deputy PM quits.
newsitem.headline: Latvians say no crisis as key deputy PM quits.

text.p: A deputy prime minister resigned from the government in the Baltic state of Latvia on Monday but political parties played down talk of a political crisis.
Ziedonis Chevers said he was quitting because Prime Minister Andris Shkele was too authoritarian and worked only for a narrow circle of big businessmen.
The small country has already been through several political crises since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991 and is now seeking political stability to pursue its economic reforms.

Chevers leads the largest group in the six-party government, the influential Democratic Party Saimnieks, but a party spokesman said his departure did not mean the whole party would leave the coalition.
"Chevers resigned as deputy prime minister and as an individual and not as a member of any political group," the spokesman told Reuters.

Shkele, a businessman with no party affiliation, was asked to head the government at the end of last year after squabbling political parties tried twice to get the backing of parliament for their own candidates.
